releases.title: Z Squared Inc. CEO David Halabu Discusses AI Data Center Strategy on Two Investor Podcasts
releases.body:
Both Interviews Are Live Now and Available Through the Company's Website and Major Podcast Platforms

FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla., Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Z Squared Inc. (Nasdaq: ZSQR) ("Z Squared" or the "Company"), a computing infrastructure company expanding into AI infrastructure, today announced that David Halabu, Chief Executive Officer, was recently featured on two investor podcasts: The Wall Street Resource, hosted by Jeff Kone, and The Nano Cap Podcast, hosted by Will Tjernlund. Both interviews are live now.

Speaking with Jeff Kone on The Wall Street Resource, Mr. Halabu outlined how Z Squared acquires existing powered sites - former crypto mining and manufacturing facilities - and retrofits them for AI and high-performance computing use. He described the Company's role as a triple-net landlord, positioned the Union County Campus in Arkansas as its flagship asset, and reiterated the two measures he has asked shareholders to hold the Company to over the next 12 to 18 months: megawatts under management and signed leases.

Speaking with Will Tjernlund on The Nano Cap Podcast, Mr. Halabu traced his background in trading and real estate and the Company's path to the public markets, and detailed the criteria Z Squared applies to a prospective site - price, power and time to power, redundant fiber, water, and county and municipal support. He also addressed the expanding role of behind-the-meter generation as utility interconnection timelines lengthen, and why he expects land and power to remain scarce as AI compute demand grows.

"These conversations were a chance to be direct about what we are building and how it generates revenue," said David Halabu, Chief Executive Officer of Z Squared. "We find power, deliver a shell an AI tenant can use, and grow the site behind it. Over the next 12 to 18 months, measure us on megawatts and leases."

The full interviews can be found via the following links:

The Wall Street Resource (Jeff Kone): Here

The Nano Cap Podcast (Will Tjernlund): Here

Both interviews touched on the Company's previously announced acquisition of Paradox Data, LLC and the Union County Campus it brought with it. Set out below are the questions investors have most frequently raised about that transaction.

What did Z Squared acquire?

Z Squared acquired 100% of the membership interests of Paradox Data, LLC, whose flagship asset is the Union County Campus in El Dorado, Arkansas. The transaction closed on an all-stock basis - no cash at closing and no debt financing.

How much power does the Union County Campus have today, and how does it scale?

The campus has an existing arrangement with Entergy Arkansas for energy service of up to 8.0 MW, plus an executed contract for adjacent land. On The Wall Street Resource, Mr. Halabu described roughly eight megawatts of total capacity and six megawatts of critical capacity available today. The development pathway targets up to 150 MW over time through a combination of utility power and on-site generation, added in phases as utility timelines and customer demand allow.

How does Z Squared expect to generate revenue from the campus?

Z Squared intends to operate as a triple-net landlord, not a compute provider: it expects to lease the land, the building and access to power to tenants - primarily "neocloud" and enterprise AI users - with power treated as a pass-through, and does not intend to buy or lease GPUs. Mr. Halabu said he is hopeful the first six to eight megawatts can be monetized in the early-to-mid 2027 timeframe, subject to the factors described under "Forward-Looking Statements" below.

About Z Squared Inc.

Z Squared Inc. is a computing infrastructure company operating advanced computing equipment and expanding into AI infrastructure. The Company's strategy is built on three principles: lead with power by acquiring operating sites where power is already flowing; build for AI workloads by converting that capacity into AI-ready colocation where the customer brings the compute and runs what they need; and scale with discipline by deploying conversion capital site by site, against signed contracts and operational readiness. Z Squared's common stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Market under the symbol "ZSQR" in April 2026.

For more information, visit www.zsquaredinc.com. 

Investor Relations Contact: ZSQR@mzgroup.us

releases.title: New Retirement in America Podcast: Rising Healthcare Costs Put Retirement Security Under Pressure
releases.body:
Segal Board Chair David Blumenstein Examines the Changing Benefits Landscape, the Enduring Value of Pensions and the Future of Retirement

WASHINGTON, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The National Institute on Retirement Security (NIRS) today released Episode 5 of its Retirement in America podcast, "The New Reality of Retirement and Workplace Benefits."

The new episode features David Blumenstein, board chair and immediate past president and CEO of Segal, and podcast host Dan Doonan in a wide-ranging conversation about the forces reshaping employee benefits and retirement security. They examine rising healthcare costs, the shift of retirement responsibility to individuals, the continuing value of pensions, changing expectations for workplace benefits, and how technology and artificial intelligence could transform the field.

Retirement in America is available on the NIRS website, YouTube, and all major podcast platforms.

"Healthcare and retirement benefits do not exist in separate silos," Doonan said. "When healthcare costs consume a larger share of compensation, there is less room for wages and retirement contributions. David brings decades of experience working with employers and plan sponsors, and this conversation helps explain why strengthening retirement security requires looking at the entire benefits landscape."

Blumenstein says the pace of change confronting employers and plan sponsors has accelerated significantly. On the retirement side, advances in computing have enabled more sophisticated risk modeling. On the healthcare side, employers are navigating rapidly evolving treatments, telehealth and other new approaches to care. At the same time, workers increasingly expect benefits information and tools to be as immediate and easy to use as other digital services.

The conversation also explores the broader shift toward placing more responsibility for saving for retirement on individual workers. Blumenstein says that while defined contribution plans are an important part of the retirement system, many workers cannot simply save more when their income is already consumed by basic necessities. Doonan and Blumenstein discuss the role defined benefit pensions can play by providing lifetime income workers can count on, as well as the need for personal savings to supplement retirement income.

Blumenstein also offers an optimistic view of technology and artificial intelligence. He expects new tools to make benefits analysis faster and more responsive while allowing employers and workers to model decisions more easily. But he emphasizes that critical thinking, problem solving and judgment will remain essential as the benefits field continues to evolve.

Among the topics discussed in the episode:

  • Rising healthcare costs and retirement security. Healthcare inflation puts pressure on employer compensation budgets, potentially leaving less available for wages and retirement benefits while workers and retirees face higher medical expenses.
  • The changing employee benefits landscape. Employers and plan sponsors are adapting to faster technological change, new healthcare treatments and rising expectations for easy, real-time access to benefits information.
  • The growing burden on individuals. Workers are increasingly responsible for saving for their own retirement, even as affordability pressures can make it difficult to maximize 401(k) or IRA contributions.
  • The enduring value of pensions. Doonan and Blumenstein discuss how defined benefit plans provide lifetime income and reduce some of the complex financial decisions and risks individuals otherwise must manage on their own.
  • Technology and AI. Blumenstein sees technology as a force that can improve modeling, communication and decision-making, while increasing the importance of critical thinking and problem solving.
  • A collective approach to retirement security. The episode closes with a discussion of the need for employers, policymakers and other stakeholders to work together on challenges that cannot be solved by individuals alone.

Retirement in America is a podcast from NIRS examining the economic, workforce and policy trends influencing retirement security. Combining expert insight with real-world experiences, the podcast helps listeners better understand one of the most important financial issues facing American workers and families today.

The National Institute on Retirement Security is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization established to contribute to informed policymaking by fostering a deep understanding of the value of retirement security to employees, employers, and the economy as a whole. Located in Washington, D.C., NIRS membership includes financial services firms, employee benefit plans, trade associations, and other retirement service providers.

releases.title: This Is Wild, WWF-Canada's hit podcast, returns with a look at the fragile future of southern resident killer whales and other species at risk
releases.body:
Hosted by award-winning filmmaker and environmental journalist Aliya Jasmine, the second season premieres Sept. 17.

TORONTO, Sept. 17, 2026 /CNW/ -- WWF-Canada's top science podcast This Is Wild returns for a second season, opening with a powerful episode about the urgent threats facing southern resident killer whales, one of Canada's most iconic species.

The season premiere revisits the story of Tahlequah, the southern resident killer whale who captured international attention in 2018 when she carried her dead calf through the Salish Sea for 17 days (a behaviour we saw again in 2025 after the tragic loss of another calf). Her journey became a symbol of this orca population in crisis and raised awareness about the immense pressures they're facing.

Declining chinook salmon populations, underwater noise from vessels and industry, and pollution are just some of the growing threats to southern resident killer whales. Today, only around 75 remain, with their future hanging in a precarious balance.

Episode 1 features WWF-Canada conservation experts Hussein Alidina and Emily Giles alongside Ecojustice lawyer Margot Venton with narration by award-winning environmental journalist Aliya Jasmine. Together they explore the science behind these threats, the conservation efforts aimed at supporting their recovery, and the legal and policy hurdles that are slowing down action and ramping up risks.

"We know better. We have to do better. It's our responsibility to do better. And we need to do that better because in many ways, we're part of the same circle of life that the whales are," said Hussein Alidina, WWF-Canada's lead specialist for marine conservation.

"Southern resident killer whales are one of the most beloved species in Canada, and one of the most endangered. At a time when Canada is accelerating approvals for major projects like ports and pipelines that risk their survival, the first episode of This is Wild asks the important question of what we're willing to lose for economic gain," said Megan Leslie, WWF-Canada's president and CEO. "Each episode takes listeners to different parts of the country, exploring the species that are shaping our world and what it will take to protect theirs."

Co-produced with Antica Productions, the second season of This Is Wild continues WWF-Canada's commitment to making conservation stories engaging and accessible.

Aliya Jasmine previously appeared on an episode of WWF-Canada's Good Nature podcast, talking about her new short documentary Bird Names.

Listen to season two of This is Wild wherever you get your podcasts. New episodes about a different incredible species that call Canada home, and the people working to protect them, will be released every two weeks. 

  • YouTube
  • Apple Podcasts
  • Spotify
  • Podlink for more streaming platforms
  • https://wwf.ca/this-is-wild/ 

For a copy of the episode transcript or to arrange an interview with our experts, email media@wwfcanada.org 

About the host, Aliya Jasmine

Aliya Jasmine ("AJ") is an award-winning filmmaker, environmental journalist and climate storyteller whose work sits at the intersection of climate solutions, wildlife and belonging. Her stories have appeared on CBC, NBC News, MTV News, Discovery Channel, and Smithsonian Channel, and she has built a large trusted online community through years of broadcast journalism, digital-first reporting and environmental storytelling.

AJ is co-Founder of Earth Tones, a purpose-driven media company amplifying underrepresented voices in environmental storytelling. AJ directed, wrote and produced Bird Names, a CBC Short Docs documentary with an impact campaign spanning private, public, academic, and conservation-facing screenings. She is also directing Lion Bridge, an independent feature documentary from Executive Producer Leonardo DiCaprio, about LA's mountain lion population, currently in production. 

She is a recipient of the King Charles III Coronation Medal for journalism in service of Canada, a Fellow of the Royal Canadian Geographical Society, and serves on the board of Nature United.

About WWF-Canada

WWF-Canada is committed to equitable and effective conservation actions that restore nature, reverse wildlife loss and fight climate change. We draw on scientific analysis and Indigenous guidance to ensure all our efforts connect to a single goal: a future where wildlife, nature and people thrive. For more information, visit wwf.ca.

SOURCE World Wildlife Fund Canada

releases.title: Bielat Santore & Company Releases Episode 6 of the Owner's Edge Podcast Series: "New Jersey Liquor Licenses: Regulatory Structure and Market Value"
releases.body:
First installment of a two-part educational series provides hospitality owners, buyers, and developers with an in-depth framework for navigating state ABC regulations, municipal population caps, Class C license privileges, and asset valuation.

ALLENHURST, N.J. , Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Commercial real estate brokerage firm Bielat Santore & Company has officially released Episode 6 (Part I) of its Owner's Edge Podcast Series, titled "New Jersey Liquor Licenses: Regulatory Structure and Market Value". The episode delivers a comprehensive analysis of how New Jersey's unique statutory framework governs retail alcoholic beverage licenses and creates private-market economic value.

Although New Jersey law classifies a liquor license as a regulated government privilege rather than ordinary property, eligible licenses command substantial market value across the state.

Key Topics Covered in Episode 6 (Part I):

  • The Statutory Framework & Municipal Population Caps: Established under Title 33 following the repeal of Prohibition in 1933, New Jersey's Alcoholic Beverage Control system ties retail licenses to local population limits.
  • Essential Class C Retail Licenses: An overview of key retail license types, including Type 33 (Plenary Retail Consumption for standard bar/restaurant service), Type 32 (Plenary Retail Consumption with Broad Package Privilege, no longer newly issued), Type 44 (Plenary Retail Distribution for package stores).
  • Person-to-Person & Place-to-Place Transfers: Clarifying the legal separation between purchasing a business asset and transferring a license.
  • The Six-Step Valuation Framework: Addressing why there is no standardized statewide price database and presenting a six-step valuation methodology.
  • Impact on Operating Economics & Real Estate: How beverage service enhances average guest checks, gross profit margins, and late-day sales.

Coming Next Month - Part II: "Recent Changes in New Jersey Liquor License Law"

About Bielat Santore & Company

Bielat Santore & Company is a New Jersey commercial real estate brokerage specializing in restaurants, hospitality properties, business enterprises, and liquor licenses. For more than 45 years, the firm has advised owners, operators, developers, buyers, and lenders on the sale, acquisition, financing, and valuation of hospitality assets throughout New Jersey.

releases.title: Planet Classroom and VoiceAmerica Launch New "Net Zero Speaks" Podcast: "We Have Everything We Need": Solar Pioneer Andrew Blakers Says the World Already Has the Technology for a 100% Clean Energy Future
releases.body:
Australian National University professor and co-inventor of PERC solar cell technology joins youth host Ivan Ransom to explain why the clean-energy transition is no longer a technological challenge—it is a matter of action.

NEW YORK, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The transition to clean energy is no longer constrained by technology—it is purely a matter of execution.

The Planet Classroom Network, in partnership with VoiceAmerica, today announces the podcast release of Net Zero Speaks to Andrew Blakers. Hosted by youth climate advocate Ivan Ransom, this briefing features Professor Andrew Blakers AO FAA FTSE FRSN of the Australian National University, one of the world's leading renewable energy researchers and co-developer of the PERC solar cell technology used in much of today's global solar industry.

At the heart of the discussion is an unequivocal message: the world already possesses the technology required to run on 100 percent renewable energy.

"We have everything we need," Blakers explains. "We don't need to invent anything. It's just a matter of getting out and doing it."

A VISION FOR CHEAP, CLEAN ENERGY FOREVER

Throughout the conversation, Blakers outlines a global future powered by what he calls "clean, cheap energy forever," noting that "most countries are their own Saudi Arabia of solar and wind."

Drawing on decades of research, he demonstrates how solar power, wind energy, pumped hydro storage, batteries, and electrification technologies can seamlessly integrate to create reliable, affordable, zero-carbon energy systems at scale worldwide.

A GLOBAL VOICE ON RENEWABLE INNOVATION

Professor Blakers is internationally recognized for helping develop the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell (PERC) solar cell—a breakthrough that dramatically increased solar panel efficiency, transformed the modern solar industry, and accelerated the dramatic decline in solar energy costs globally.

Today, Blakers leads research on large-scale renewable energy systems and the Global Pumped Hydro Atlas, which identifies hundreds of thousands of potential energy storage sites capable of supporting fully renewable electricity grids.

Key insights highlighted in the episode include:

  • The Scale of Solar & Wind: Why most nations possess more than enough renewable resources to achieve total energy independence.
  • Overcoming Misconceptions: Tackling persistent myths regarding land use, raw materials, grid stability, and waste management.
  • Deep Decarbonization: How governments, utilities, and communities can achieve deep decarbonization while maintaining lower energy costs and grid reliability.

FROM SOLAR PANELS TO "GRAVITY BATTERIES"

A central focus of the episode is solving the energy storage puzzle. Blakers explains how pumped hydro systems—often described as giant "gravity batteries"—store renewable energy by moving water between two reservoirs at different elevations.

His team's research identified approximately 820,000 potential pumped hydro sites globally, offering vastly more storage capacity than needed for a fully renewable energy future. The discussion explores how these systems balance solar and wind generation while maintaining grid reliability and affordability.

"Professor Blakers reminds us that many of the critical solutions we need already exist," said C. M. (Cathy) Rubin, Co-Founder and CEO of Planet Classroom. "Understanding that we already have the tools to solve these challenges is empowering for young people. The challenge now is accelerating action and building the political and social will to implement them globally."

LISTEN TO THE EPISODE

Net Zero Speaks to Andrew Blakers premieres September 16, 2026, on VoiceAmerica and major podcast platforms via the Planet Classroom Network.

releases.title: Your Muscles May Be One of Your Most Valuable Retirement Assets
releases.body:
Fitness & Finance co-founders explain why preserving muscle should be part of the retirement-planning conversation

FREDERICKSBURG, Va., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- When it comes to retirement planning, most people focus on how much to save and where to invest it. But another asset can have an enormous influence on how those retirement years are lived: muscle. Maintaining strength and muscle mass as we age can help support mobility, balance and independence—factors that can influence both quality of life and healthcare needs later in life. The good news is that it is never too late to start investing in physical strength.

"We spend decades building a financial portfolio for retirement, but we should be building our physical portfolio at the same time," said Jennifer Scherer, co-founder of the Fitness & Finance Radio podcast, registered dietitian, medical exercise specialist, certified personal trainer, master-level Pilates instructor and founder of Fredericksburg Fitness Studio. "Muscle is one of the assets that helps protect our ability to move, remain independent and enjoy the life we worked so hard to build. Financial longevity means much less if our physical health doesn't allow us to enjoy it."

While people are focused on building their financial portfolio, they may be overlooking their physical one. Age-related losses in muscle and strength can affect mobility, balance and independence and are associated with greater risk of falls and hospitalization. Those health consequences can also create significant expenses during retirement.

According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), starting at around 30, our bodies naturally begin losing muscle mass. We lose 3-5% of muscle mass every decade, and while that change may happen slowly, it adds up, leaving people with weakened strength. Sarcopenia, the gradual loss of muscle mass, increases the risks of falls, broken bones, and hospitalization. These are all things that are going to dip into the financial savings that someone has accumulated for retirement.

A study published in the Journal of Frailty & Aging reports that the hospitalization costs associated with sarcopenia are around $40 billion. They report that those with the condition are more likely to be hospitalized, with it costing each person an average of over $2,300 per year. Add to that the costs that people incur outside of the hospital due to broken bones, falls, and any hired help they need due to the lack of independence. It adds up to a financial burden that people may have been able to avoid if they had worked on maintaining muscle mass over the years.

The key is to start working on building and maintaining muscle mass, regardless of what age someone is at. It's never too late to take this issue on. According to the NIH, 30% of adults over the age of 70 have trouble walking, getting up from a chair, or climbing stairs. They report that such mobility issues not only lead to a loss of independence, but are also linked to higher rates of falls, chronic diseases, nursing home admissions, and mortality. They report that the big culprit is a loss of muscle mass, and that it can be slowed down by maintaining an active lifestyle.

Here are some tips to keep in mind to help slow the muscle-mass loss problem:

  • Get active no matter what age you are. Know that you can always start slow and build it up as you get stronger. Being physically active is crucial to healthier aging.
  • Ensure that your workout routine has you lifting weights and challenging yourself. It's important to get things in there like resistance exercises. Include progressive resistance training. Muscles need an appropriate challenge to adapt and remain strong. Resistance can come from weights, machines, bands or body weight, and the program should be appropriate for the individual's health, abilities and experience.
  • Be sure to get the right foods in your diet in order to build and maintain muscle. Getting enough protein is a must in order to build and maintain muscle mass over the years. Know how much you need per day and pay attention to ensure you get it. Prioritize adequate nutrition, particularly protein. Protein provides the amino acids needed to support muscle maintenance and repair, but individual needs vary based on age, health status and activity level.
  • If you have one day that you slip or one week where you falter on your new fitness plans, don't give up. Just start again. Too often, people throw in the towel and give up, rather than simply getting back at it. Working with someone, such as a coach or trainer, can help keep you on track.
  • Build a professional team. A qualified fitness or healthcare professional can assess physical function and help create an appropriate plan for maintaining strength and mobility, while a qualified financial professional can help prepare for the financial realities of retirement. Both plans should support the same goal: maintaining independence and quality of life for as long as possible.

"One of the biggest expenses in retirement can be needing help with the things you once did independently," said Jeff Smith, co-founder of Fitness & Finance Radio, financial planning expert, personal trainer, master-level Pilates instructor and founder of The Retirement Smith. "We can build a strong financial plan, but preserving the physical ability to enjoy those years is equally important. Financial planning and fitness planning have more in common than people realize: both benefit from starting early, being consistent and thinking long-term."

Smith and Scherer co-founded Fitness & Finance Radio to explore an often-overlooked connection: the relationship between physical health and financial health throughout the lifespan. Drawing on Scherer's expertise in nutrition, medical exercise and fitness and Smith and Scherer are a married couple who co-founded the Fitness & Finance Radio podcast, where they come together to share their fields of expertise. The information focuses on offering a mix of nutrition, healthy lifestyle, and financial retirement planning strategies. Listeners can tune in to hear the duo discuss the issues and gain advice and insight that may help them now and in their retirement years. The Fitness & Finance Radio podcast is available for free on YouTube. Recent episode topics cover credibility, stress, funding adult children, saving money and losing weight on vacation, obesity and preventative care, and more. To get more information and listen, visit the site at: https://www.youtube.com/@fitnessfinanceradio?app=desktop

releases.title: Public Service Announcement - Canadian War Museum launches The Long War, a podcast exploring Canada's role in the Afghanistan war
releases.body:
OTTAWA, ON, Sept. 10, 2026 /CNW/ -- In the wake of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks against the United States, Canada joined the U.S.-led invasion of Afghanistan to pursue al-Qaeda and unseat the Taliban. More than 40,000 Canadians served. Over the course of the war, more than 1,500 were wounded and a diplomat and 158 Canadian soldiers died. Now, 25 years later, the Canadian War Museum is launching a new podcast that delves into the history and legacy of this overseas mission, which forever marked Canadian military history.

The Long War: Canada in Afghanistan offers a compelling examination of Canada's 13-year mission. Hosted by journalist Anna Maria Tremonti and guided by War Museum historian Andrew Burtch, the series traces the arc of Canada's role in the conflict -- from early victories and attempts to build a democratic state, to the counterinsurgency and the final fall of Kabul. It revisits key moments from the war, while also exploring its complicated legacy.

The series incorporates historical documentary recordings, War Museum oral histories, and original interviews conducted for the podcast. Listeners will hear from military leaders, diplomats, veterans, and policymakers, including former Chief of the Defence Staff General (Ret'd) Wayne Eyre; Major-General (Ret'd) David Fraser; Elissa Golberg, the Representative of Canada in Kandahar in 2009, and current Canadian Ambassador to Italy; and former Cabinet minister and Deputy Prime Minister John Manley. By focusing on the voices of the people who were there, the podcast combines powerful firsthand storytelling with thoughtful reflection upon a defining chapter in Canadian military history.

Eight episodes cover the history and legacy chronologically:

  • The Fall and the Beginning
  • Into Battle (2001–2002)
  • Defence, Diplomacy, Development (2003–2006)
  • Operation Medusa (2006)
  • Home Front (2006–2008)
  • The Grind (2007–2010)
  • A Long Goodbye (2010–2014)
  • Reckoning

Full descriptions and links are available on the Museum website, and on all major podcast platforms. The first episode is available today; the remaining episodes will be released weekly over the next two months.

The Long War: Canada in Afghanistan will be launched September 10 at the War Museum, with a special in-person panel discussion featuring some of the people interviewed for the podcast. Tickets can be purchased from the War Museum website. This event is presented in conjunction with The World at War Speaker Series, an annual program of compelling lectures presented by the War Museum. A list of upcoming events is also available.

This year also marks the fifth anniversary of the collapse of the Afghan government to the Taliban, and the 20th anniversary of Operation Medusa, one of the toughest battles in Afghanistan for both the Canadian Army and NATO.

Many voices heard in The Long War come from the War Museum's oral history project, In Their Own Voices: Stories From Canadian Veterans and Their Loved Ones. Both of these projects have been generously funded by donors including the A. Britton Smith Family; the Azrieli Foundation; Arthur B.C. Drache, C.M., K.C., and Judy Young Drache; The Royal Canadian Legion; The Legion National Foundation; Friends of the Canadian War Museum; the Crabtree Foundation; Robert Stollery, in honour of his service in the Second World War; Colonel (Ret'd) Stanley A. Milner, O.C., A.O.E., M.S.M., C.D., LL.D.; and individuals from across Canada.

The Canadian War Museum is Canada's national museum of military history. Its mission is to promote public understanding of Canada's military history in its personal, national and international dimensions.

For more information, visit warmuseum.ca. Follow us on Twitter, Facebook or Instagram.

If you would like to have your name removed from our distribution list or if this information should be directed to someone else, please send an email to Avra Gibbs Lamey.

WASHINGTON, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The White House Historical Association today released a new episode of The White House 1600 Sessions podcast marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks through firsthand accounts from three people who experienced the fateful day from inside the White House and alongside President George W. releases.title: NEW Episode: The White House 1600 Sessions Podcast "Inside the White House on September 11"
releases.body:
White House Historical Association President

Stewart McLaurin Reflects on September 11, 2001,

25 Years Later with Former ABC News White House Correspondent Ann Compton,

Longtime White House Chief Usher Gary Walters, and Former Special Assistant to

President George W. Bush Anita McBride

WASHINGTON, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The White House Historical Association today released a new episode of The White House 1600 Sessions podcast marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks through firsthand accounts from three people who experienced the fateful day from inside the White House and alongside President George W. Bush.

President of the White House Historical Association, Stewart McLaurin sits down with former ABC News White House correspondent Ann Compton; Gary Walters, the longtime White House chief usher; and Anita McBride, then special assistant to President George W. Bush. Their first-person accounts offer a rare look inside the White House on September 11 and preserve these important memories for future generations.

President George W. Bush began that morning at an elementary school in Sarasota, Florida. Within minutes, he was leading the nation through one of the gravest crises in its history. As officials rushed him aboard Air Force One, White House staff evacuated the complex amid reports that another hijacked aircraft could be heading toward Washington. Throughout the day, those at the White House worked to maintain continuity of government while preparing for the president's return.

After evacuating the White House, McBride details how she led her colleagues to a nearby office building so White House staff could have access to the technology they needed to continue working and supporting the Executive Mansion.

Gary Walters details how he remained at the White House to prepare for the President's return as South Lawn was set up for a picnic and needed to be cleared for Marine One to land upon the President's arrival home.

"Six of us got around the picnic tables and picked them up one by one and carried them over to the roadway and stacked them one on top of the other," said Walters. "We also had to take up the floor of the stage, everything that was moveable had to go. It was a massive undertaking and exhausting, but the exhilaration and the adrenaline was flowing in everybody."

Ann Compton recounts her experience as a member of the press pool travelling with the president.  From Florida to Louisiana, Nebraska, and ultimately back to Washington, D.C., she witnessed the president's movements firsthand and offered unique insight into his response and actions on September 11.

"While the president was listening to the children, I suddenly saw Andy Card, the White House Chief of Staff, come quickly in, lean over, whisper to the president, and quickly step back again. What stunned me was the look on the president's face," said Compton. "He had been president for less than nine months, and I had never seen President Bush with a look of such gravity, iron gravity in his eyes."

McLaurin, Compton, McBride, and Walters also reflect on the leadership, humanity, and national unity that emerged from one of the darkest days in American history. They also discuss the importance of preserving these firsthand memories for generations with no living memory of September 11.

"Political affiliations seemed to fade away," said McLaurin. "I remember so vividly, Congress on the steps of the Capitol that night singing together, united, and the president going to New York in the subsequent days."

"People banded together," said McBride. "That's the message of September 11, the humanity and the unity that we felt in our darkest hour, and that's what defines who we are as an American people."

The White House 1600 Sessions podcast is available on Apple Podcasts and Spotify.

The full video of this podcast episode is also available on the White House Historical Association's YouTube channel here.

The White House 1600 Sessions 

The White House Historical Association's President Stewart McLaurin is the host of The White House 1600 Sessions, the Association's official audio and video podcast devoted to exploring the history, cultural impact, untold stories, and personal accounts of America's most iconic residence and highest office.

About the White House Historical Association 

Founded in 1961 by First Lady Jacqueline Kennedy, the White House Historical Association is the nonprofit, nonpartisan organization entrusted with preserving and sharing the history of the White House. Supported entirely by private philanthropy and the sale of educational books and products, the Association reaches millions of students, teachers, and lifelong learners through research and scholarship initiatives, public programming, and the authoritative titles published by its independent press. Throughout each presidency, the Association works with the Offices of the First Lady and the White House Curator to acquire and preserve historic objects for the White House Fine and Decorative Arts Collection. The Association also operates The People's House: A White House Experience, a free, immersive, educational museum in Washington, D.C., which welcomes hundreds of thousands of visitors annually. To learn more about the White House Historical Association, please visit WhiteHouseHistory.org.

releases.title: Blubrry Brings Unified Video and Audio Podcast Publishing to Apple Podcasts
releases.body:
Blubrry Publisher customers can upload one video episode and make it available to watch or listen through a single podcast feed

COOPERSVILLE, Mich., Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Blubrry Podcasting today announced that it now works with Apple Podcasts to integrate HTTP Live Streaming (HLS) video into shows published through Blubrry Publisher.

The new workflow allows Blubrry hosting customers to upload one MP4 video episode and make it available in video and audio formats through a single RSS feed. Blubrry automatically creates an HLS video version for Apple Podcasts, retains the original video file and generates an MP3 audio version for podcast apps that do not support HLS video.

For creators, this means one upload, one episode and one feed to manage. For audiences using Apple Podcasts, it provides the flexibility to watch or listen and switch between audio and video with a tap.

"Video podcasting should give creators more ways to share their work without requiring a separate publishing process," said Barry Kantz, CEO at Blubrry Podcasting. "Blubrry Publisher customers can upload one video episode, continue managing one podcast feed and give their audience the choice to watch or listen."

A More Flexible Experience on Apple Podcasts

Video on Apple Podcasts uses HTTP Live Streaming video. HLS video divides an episode into smaller segments and prepares it at multiple quality levels.

As someone watches, Apple Podcasts can adjust the video quality based on the strength of their Wi-Fi or cellular connection. This adaptive delivery can help video begin playing faster and continue with fewer buffering interruptions as connection conditions change.

Because video and audio are connected to the same episode, audiences can switch between audio and video with a tap without searching for another version of the show.

One Upload, Three Available Formats

When a Blubrry Publisher customer uploads an MP4 video episode, Blubrry automatically prepares:

  • An HLS video version for Apple Podcasts
  • The original uploaded video file
  • An MP3 audio version for audio-focused podcast apps

All three formats are included within the same RSS feed.

Apple Podcasts uses the HLS video version. Other podcast apps can use the HLS video, original video file or MP3 audio enclosure based on the formats they support.

This removes the need to upload separate audio and video episodes or maintain parallel feeds for the same show.

Available Through Blubrry Publisher

After connecting Apple Podcasts Connect to Blubrry, customers can publish video episodes through their existing Blubrry Publisher workflow.

Blubrry automatically prepares the uploaded video as a 1080p Full HD HLS video version and creates an MP3 audio version. Some processing time is required before the episode becomes available to watch on Apple Podcasts.

The feature is currently available to Blubrry hosting customers using Blubrry Publisher. It is not available for shows published through the PowerPress podcasting plugin at this time.

PowerPress customers can continue using their current WordPress publishing workflow without making any changes.

To get started, customers must generate an API key through Apple Podcasts Connect and upload the key file within their Blubrry dashboard.

Customers can learn more at HLS at Blubrry or follow the setup instructions in Blubrry's documentation.

About Blubrry Podcasting

Blubrry Podcasting provides podcast hosting, publishing, audience statistics, monetization and distribution tools for audio and video creators. Its services include Blubrry Publisher, the PowerPress podcasting plugin for WordPress, IAB-certified podcast statistics, podcast websites and tools for independent creators, businesses and podcast networks.

releases.title: Martin Guitar Launches Martin Stories, a New, Artist-Focused Podcast
releases.body:
The official Martin Guitar podcast, hosted by Jimmy Leslie, explores the music, creativity, instruments, and personal journeys behind some of today's most compelling artists

NAZARETH, Pa., Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- C. F. Martin & Co.® today announced the launch of Martin Stories, the official podcast of Martin Guitar and a new destination for conversations with the artists, players, collectors, and creators who have a Martin guitar at the center of their musical lives.

Hosted by Jimmy Leslie, Frets Acoustic Editor at Guitar Player, Martin Stories goes beyond the music to explore the careers artists have built, the moments that shaped them, the instruments they have connected with along the way, and the hard-won insights that come from a lifetime of playing and creating.

Every Martin owner has a story. For nearly 200 years, Martin guitars have been part of countless musical journeys—from songs written at home to performances heard around the world. Martin Stories brings those journeys to the forefront, creating a place where artists can share their stories about the moments built around that unmistakable Martin tone.

The Stories Behind the Sound

Each episode of Martin Stories takes listeners inside an artist's relationship with music and the instruments that have helped shape it. Conversations span creativity, influences, collecting, songwriting, touring, career-defining moments, and the personal stories that can turn a guitar into far more than a musical instrument.

The first two episodes are available now.

The debut episode, released August 12, features Kenneth Pattengale of The Milk Carton Kids. Pattengale joins Leslie from his North Hollywood studio to trace the story of his main guitar, a 1954 Martin 0-15 he first encountered in a museum case and spent more than two years searching for before eventually using it as the inspiration for his own Martin signature model.

Their conversation explores Pattengale's approach to creating The Milk Carton Kids' distinctive two-guitar sound, his attraction to instruments that feel authentic rather than pristine, the unexpected origins of his accessible signature guitar, and what thousands of performances have taught him about choosing connection over perfection.

The second episode, released August 26, welcomes blues guitarist Joe Bonamassa, whose Martin story began as a child playing his father's mid-1970s D-35 in the vintage guitar shop where he grew up.

From "Nerdville Gotham," his New York City home and vintage gear hub, Bonamassa discusses the path from that first Martin to seeing his own name inside one. The conversation explores the vintage 1937 00-18 that inspired his latest Martin signature models, his fascination with pre-war instruments, memorable guitars and performances from throughout his career, and what decades of recording, touring, and collecting have taught him about finding the right instrument.

More Martin Stories to Come

New episodes of Martin Stories will arrive every two weeks, with upcoming guests including Don Felder, Brooke Ligertwood, Eric Johnson, and many more artists from across the musical landscape.

The podcast is hosted by Jimmy Leslie, Frets Acoustic Editor at Guitar Player and a Bay Area-based writer, guitarist, and vocalist who records and performs original music as Spirit Hustler and under his own name.

Martin Stories is produced by Elizabeth Evans Media.

Martin Stories is available to stream now on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, YouTube, and other major podcast platforms.

For more information about Martin Guitar, visit martinguitar.com.

ABOUT C. F. MARTIN & CO.

C. F. Martin & Co. has been making the finest handcrafted acoustic guitars for nearly two hundred years. For some of the biggest names and the most revered musical legends across every genre and every decade. And we've been doing it with pure artistic passion, a deep love for all things music, and an unwavering commitment to our community and the environment.

But most importantly, we're still doing it... for you. For current and future generations of pioneers, rebels, and dreamers. For the beginners, the pros, and everyone in between. We believe music is an unstoppable force. It raises us up. Tells our truths. Gets us on our feet. Expresses our deepest heartaches. And our greatest joys.

So, we'll continue to make the very best acoustic instruments and strings for as long as there are people like you who love music and love making it. We want to be there to help you tell your story. To help you share your music with the world. To help unleash the artist within.

We're ready for the next two hundred years. Want to come with us? Visit martinguitar.com.

releases.title: Marie-Mai hosts L'Accolade, Leucan's new podcast
releases.body:
A platform for families to share their experiences with pediatric cancer

MONTRÉAL, Sept. 1, 2026 /CNW/ -- Leucan and Marie-Mai are proud to announce the launch of L'Accolade, Leucan's new French-language podcast. The four-episode series features conversations with adolescents, young adults and parents about their experiences with pediatric cancer. All four episodes of L'Accolade are now available in French on Leucan's website and YouTube channel, as well as on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

Marie-Mai, Leucan's spokesperson since 2016, hosts each hour-long episode. The launch coincides with the beginning of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, observed each September.

L'Accolade addresses the wide-ranging impacts of pediatric cancer, including psychosocial needs, financial insecurity, clinical research, self-esteem, resilience, and the loss of a child.

"As Leucan's spokesperson for the past 10 years, I have had the privilege of meeting many families, and every encounter has stayed with me in a different way," says Marie-Mai. "I wanted to deepen my commitment through a project that would allow me to listen--to understand how pediatric cancer can change a family and a life. Despite the seriousness of the issues discussed, what has struck me most is the remarkable strength and spirit of these families. Beyond the lasting effects of illness, I wanted their voices to be heard."

A resource for families affected by pediatric cancer

The title L'Accolade, French for "the embrace," reflects Leucan's commitment to supporting families without judgment at every stage of their journey.

Juli Meilleur, Leucan's executive director, is featured in one episode. As the mother of a child who has recovered from three cancers, she brings both professional and personal perspectives to the conversation.

"Pediatric cancer is often discussed through statistics or fundraising campaigns. With this podcast, we are giving a face and a voice to the realities we encounter every day at Leucan," says Meilleur. "I also take part as a Leucan parent. From the moment a diagnosis is announced, families often need to hear from others who have been through a similar journey. That is the space we have created with this podcast."

Four episodes, four inspiring stories

  • Episode 1: Turning adversity into a mission, with Juli Meilleur
  • Episode 2: Cancer, blindness and a new country: rebuilding as a teenager, with Anoushka
  • Episode 3: Research, resilience and laughter, with Véronic
  • Episode 4: Facing the unimaginable: the loss of a child, with Sabrina-Claudia

About Leucan

For more than 48 years, Leucan has supported children with cancer and their families from the time of diagnosis and throughout every stage of the illness. Through a qualified team with recognized expertise in pediatric cancer, the Association provides specialized, tailored services to hundreds of families and thousands of members across Quebec.

Leucan also funds clinical research and operates the Leucan Information Centre, helping families access reliable information and support throughout their child's cancer journey. With seven offices across the province, Leucan is there for families throughout Quebec.

SOURCE Leucan

releases.title: "As Apple Podcasts move into Video, Santa Monica Studios Launches Live-Edited TV-Quality Podcast Production Model"
releases.body:
New studio workflow allows creators to produce television‑quality live-edited podcasts with dramatically lower production costs

SANTA MONICA, Calif., Aug. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- With over 1 billion people watching podcast content on YouTube each month, the major platforms are rapidly adapting to this shift toward visual podcasting.

Apple begins rolling out a video-podcast experience built directly into the Apple Podcasts app with upcoming iOS updates. The move signals a major industry shift.

"The media landscape is shifting," said Magnus Ohman, Head of Podcasting at Santa Monica Studios. "Podcasts are no longer just audio. With elections being influenced by podcasts and awards shows like the Golden Globes recognizing podcasting as its own category, the format has become one of the most powerful platforms where authentic voices can be heard."

Faster Growth Than Traditional Media

Podcasting is now one of the fastest‑growing media industries:

  • Podcast industry growth: 15–30% annually
  • Film industry growth: 2–4%
  • Television industry growth: 1–2%

New technology makes high-level production cost-effective

Using live editing, AI-assisted green-screen technology, and real-time production workflows, the studio can produce broadcast-quality content while dramatically reducing post-production costs. Episodes can be delivered almost immediately after recording, allowing creators to produce television‑quality content at a fraction of the traditional production cost. 

This approach allows creators to generate material that works across multiple platforms, including streaming television, FAST channels, YouTube, podcast platforms, and social media.

FAST TV has become the fastest‑growing television segment in the United States, creating new opportunities for creators to distribute hybrid podcast‑TV shows to global audiences.

"FAST television is opening an entirely new distribution channel for creators," said Konstantin Stepanov, Head of Production at Santa Monica Studios. "Creators can produce content that works simultaneously as a podcast, a television show, and short‑form video across multiple platforms."

A Full‑Service Production Platform for Creators

Santa Monica Studios provides production for established creators, including Maria Shriver, Tamsen Fadal, and Ramit Sethi, while also serving as a full‑service podcast and TV show production studio for companies, entrepreneurs, and creators launching new products or ideas.

"Our goal is to help creators take their ideas and turn them into high‑quality shows that can live across podcast platforms, streaming television, and social media," says Leana Greene, director and producer at Santa Monica Studios. "With live editing and studio‑level production, creators can produce premium content without the traditional cost of television production."

About Santa Monica Studios

Santa Monica Studios is a full-service production facility specializing in television production, podcasts and TV shows, live-edited broadcast content, commercials, documentaries, corporate videos, brand videos, green screen, PSAs, editing, and post-production. The studio has LTN live broadcast capability and can stream to any Network. The studio combines cinema-grade equipment, AI-assisted production workflows, and experienced crews to help creators and companies produce high-quality content in a cost-effective way.
